hero.eyebrow: Calendar sync for people with more than one calendar
hero.title: One schedule. Every calendar.
hero.subtitle: Mirror events from your work, personal and family calendars into each other, with full details or as private “Busy” blocks. Nobody double-books you again.

how.title: Set up in about a minute
how.subtitle: Three steps, then it runs on its own.
how.step1Body: Add as many Google accounts as your plan allows: work, personal, a shared family calendar.
how.step2Body: Pick a source calendar, a target calendar, and how much detail the copy should carry.
how.step3Body: New, moved and cancelled events are mirrored within seconds via push notifications, with a safety-net check every few minutes.

modes.title: Full details or just “Busy”. Your call, per rule.
modes.subtitle: Share what you want, hide what you don't.
modes.fullBody: Title, description, location and the guest list (as text) are copied. Ideal between your own calendars.
modes.busyBody: An opaque, private block with no details. Colleagues see you're unavailable, and nothing else.
modes.twoWayBody: Create two rules in opposite directions. Loop protection makes sure mirrors are never mirrored back.

privacy.title: Built to be trusted with your calendar
privacy.tokensBody: Google access tokens are encrypted at rest with AES-256-GCM and never leave our servers.
privacy.contentBody: We keep only event ids and a fingerprint to detect changes. Titles and descriptions pass through, they are not kept.
privacy.openBody: The code is AGPL-3.0 licensed. Read it, audit it, or run your own instance.
privacy.noInvitesBody: Mirrors never carry attendees and have reminders turned off, so nobody gets an email and you never get a double notification.

pricingTeaser.title: Simple pricing
pricingTeaser.subtitle: Start with a 7-day free trial. Pick the plan that fits how many calendars you juggle.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.a1: Google Calendar today, including Google Workspace accounts and calendars shared with you. Microsoft 365 and iCloud are on the roadmap.
faq.q2: Will my colleagues see my private appointments?
faq.a2: Only if you choose “Full details”. With “Busy only” they see an opaque block marked private, with no title, description or location.
faq.q3: What happens if I create rules in both directions?
faq.a3: That's a two-way sync, and it's safe: every mirror is tagged, and tagged events are never mirrored again.
faq.q4: Do guests get invitations from the mirrored events?
faq.a4: No. Mirrors never include attendees; in full-details mode the guest list is added to the description as text.
faq.q5: What happens when my trial ends?
faq.a5: Your card is charged and syncing continues. If you cancel, syncing pauses and your data is kept for 30 days in case you come back. Mirrored events already in your calendars stay where they are.
faq.a6: Yes. The project is open source; you need Postgres, an SMTP server and your own Google OAuth app.

finalCta.title: Stop copying events by hand
finalCta.subtitle: Connect your first calendar in under a minute.

legal.privacyIntro: This policy explains how {brand}, operated by {entity}, processes personal data when you use the hosted service, in line with the EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), the UK GDPR and Brazil's Lei Geral de Proteção de Dados (LGPD, Law 13.709/2018). Self-hosted instances are operated, and controlled, by whoever runs them.

privacySections.title: Who is responsible (controller)
paragraphs: The controller of your personal data is {entity}.
Registered address: {address}.
Our Data Protection Officer (Encarregado pelo tratamento de dados pessoais, under the LGPD) is {dpo}, reachable at {privacyEmail}.
You can reach us about any privacy matter at {privacyEmail}.
Our representative in the European Union (Article 27 GDPR) is {euRep}.

privacySections.title: Personal data we process
paragraphs: Account data: your name, email address, time zone, language and, if you sign in with Google, your profile picture.
Connected calendar accounts: the email address of each Google account you connect and the OAuth tokens Google issues to us, encrypted at rest with AES-256-GCM.
Calendar metadata: identifiers, names, colors and access level of the calendars in the accounts you connect.

Sync bookkeeping: for each mirrored event, its identifiers, start and end time and a one-way fingerprint (SHA-256) used to detect changes. We do not store event titles, descriptions, locations or guest lists: they pass through our servers only while a mirror is written.
Activity logs: when each sync ran, what it changed (counts only) and error codes.
Billing data: Stripe customer and subscription identifiers, plan and status. Card details are collected and stored by Stripe, never by us.
Technical data: IP address and user agent in session records and server logs, used for security.
Consent records: your cookie choices and when you made them.
Optional, only with your consent: error reports from your browser and product-usage events linked to a pseudonymous identifier.

privacySections.title: Why we process it and our legal bases
paragraphs: To provide the service you signed up for (create your account, sign you in, read and write the calendars you choose, send transactional emails such as sign-in links): performance of a contract (GDPR Art. 6(1)(b); LGPD Art. 7, V).

To keep the service secure and reliable (session security, rate limiting, abuse prevention, server-side error monitoring without personal identifiers): our legitimate interests (GDPR Art. 6(1)(f); LGPD Art. 7, IX). You can object at any time.
To bill your subscription and keep accounting and tax records: performance of a contract and compliance with legal obligations (GDPR Art. 6(1)(b) and (c); LGPD Art. 7, II and V).

Browser error monitoring and product analytics: your consent (GDPR Art. 6(1)(a); ePrivacy rules; LGPD Art. 7, I). They stay off unless you opt in, and you can withdraw consent at any time in Cookie settings without affecting earlier processing.
Optional notification emails (for example, when a connected account needs attention): legitimate interests; you can turn them off in Settings.
We do not sell personal data, do not use it for advertising and do not make decisions about you based solely on automated processing that produce legal or similarly significant effects.

privacySections.title: Google user data
paragraphs: We request access to Google Calendar only to provide the feature you configure: reading events from the calendars you choose as a source and creating, updating or deleting mirrored events in the calendars you choose as a target. We never send invitations: mirrored events have no attendees and no reminders.

{brand}'s use and transfer to any other app of information received from Google APIs will adhere to the Google API Services User Data Policy, including the Limited Use requirements. We do not use Google user data for advertising, do not sell it, do not use it to train artificial intelligence or machine learning models, and no human reads it unless you ask us to (for support), it is necessary for security, or it is required by law.

privacySections.title: Cookies
paragraphs: We use strictly necessary cookies and local storage (sign-in session, security, language and display preferences, your consent choice). Optional technologies run only if you accept them. Our Cookie Policy lists every cookie, and Cookie settings in the footer lets you change your choice at any time.

privacySections.title: Who we share data with
paragraphs: We use service providers (processors) that act only on our instructions under data processing agreements: application hosting, a managed PostgreSQL database, transactional email delivery, payments (Stripe), and, only with your consent for the browser, error monitoring (Sentry) and product analytics (PostHog). Google receives the calendar operations you configure. The current list of sub-processors is available on request at {privacyEmail}.
We may disclose data when required by law or to protect rights and safety, and to a successor if the service is transferred, in which case you will be notified.

privacySections.title: International transfers
paragraphs: Some providers process data outside your country, including in the United States. For transfers from the EEA, UK or Switzerland we rely on adequacy decisions (including the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework where the provider is certified) or on the European Commission's Standard Contractual Clauses. For transfers from Brazil we rely on the mechanisms of LGPD Article 33, including the standard contractual clauses approved by the ANPD. You can request a copy of the relevant safeguards at {privacyEmail}.

privacySections.title: How long we keep data
paragraphs: Account, connection, calendar and rule data: while your account exists.
Sync activity logs: 90 days. Records of mirrors we removed: 30 days.
If your subscription ends: syncing pauses and your connections, rules and logs are deleted 30 days later.
When you delete your account: we revoke our access to your Google accounts and delete your data from our database right away; encrypted backups expire within 7 days.

Billing records are kept for the period required by tax and accounting law. A hashed (non-reversible) form of your email is kept for up to 1 year after account deletion only to prevent repeated free trials.
Consent records: while your account exists; the cookie storing your choice expires after 6 months, when we ask again.

privacySections.title: Your rights
paragraphs: Under the GDPR you have the right to access, rectify, erase, restrict and port your data, to object to processing based on legitimate interests, to withdraw consent at any time, and not to be subject to solely automated decisions.

Under the LGPD (Art. 18) you have the right to confirmation that we process your data; access; correction of incomplete, inaccurate or outdated data; anonymization, blocking or deletion of unnecessary or excessive data; portability; deletion of data processed with your consent; information about the entities we share data with; information about the possibility of not giving consent and its consequences; and revocation of consent.

You can exercise most rights yourself: edit your profile in Settings, download your data (Settings → Privacy → Download my data), change cookie choices (Cookie settings) and delete your account (Settings → Danger zone). For anything else, email {privacyEmail}. We may need to verify your identity, and we respond within the legal deadlines (15 days for a complete access request under the LGPD; one month under the GDPR).

privacySections.title: Complaints
paragraphs: Please contact us first so we can help. You also have the right to lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority: in Brazil, the Autoridade Nacional de Proteção de Dados (ANPD, www.gov.br/anpd); in the EEA, the data protection authority of your country of residence, work or the place of the alleged infringement; in the UK, the Information Commissioner's Office (ico.org.uk).

privacySections.title: Security
paragraphs: Data is encrypted in transit with TLS. OAuth tokens are encrypted at rest and never sent to your browser. Access to production systems is restricted to the people who operate the service, and we would notify you and the competent authorities of a personal data breach where the law requires.

privacySections.title: Children
paragraphs: {brand} is intended for adults (18+). We do not knowingly process data of children or adolescents. If you believe a minor has created an account, contact {privacyEmail} and we will delete it.

privacySections.title: Changes to this policy
paragraphs: We will publish any change on this page with a new date and, for material changes, notify you by email before they take effect. Where a change requires your consent, we will ask for it.

legal.termsIntro: These terms govern your use of the hosted {brand} service operated by {entity}. By creating an account you agree to them. If you use {brand} on behalf of an organization, you accept them for that organization.

termsSections.title: The service
paragraphs: {brand} mirrors events between calendars you connect, according to the sync rules you create. You decide which calendars are read and which are written.

termsSections.title: Eligibility and your account
paragraphs: You must be at least 18 years old and able to enter into a binding contract. Provide an email address you control and keep access to it secure. You are responsible for the activity on your account and for having the right to connect each calendar account you add.

termsSections.title: Subscriptions, free trial and payments
paragraphs: Paid plans are billed monthly in US dollars through Stripe. New subscribers get a 7-day free trial; a card is required to start it and is charged when the trial ends unless you cancel before then. One free trial per person.
Subscriptions renew automatically each month until cancelled. You can cancel anytime from the billing page; you keep access until the end of the paid period.
We may change prices with at least 30 days' notice by email; changes apply from your next billing period, and you may cancel before they take effect.

termsSections.title: Your consumer rights and refunds
paragraphs: Nothing in these terms limits rights you have under mandatory consumer law where you live.

If you are a consumer in the EU, EEA or UK, you may withdraw from a paid subscription within 14 days of the first charge; if you are a consumer in Brazil, you may exercise the right of regret (direito de arrependimento) within 7 days under Article 49 of the Consumer Defense Code. To do so, email {email}; we will refund the charge to your original payment method.
Outside these cases, fees already paid for a billing period are not refunded, except where required by law.

termsSections.title: Acceptable use
paragraphs: Do not use {brand} to access calendars you are not authorized to use, to disrupt the service or the calendar providers, to circumvent plan limits, to reverse engineer the hosted service's security controls, or for anything unlawful.

termsSections.title: Your data and privacy
paragraphs: You keep all rights to your calendar data. You authorize us to read and write it solely to operate the sync you configure. How we process personal data, including your rights under the GDPR and the LGPD, is described in our Privacy Policy, which forms part of these terms.

termsSections.title: Third-party services
paragraphs: {brand} depends on calendar providers such as Google and on payment processors such as Stripe. Their terms apply to your use of their services, and changes or outages on their side can affect syncing.

termsSections.title: Availability and changes
paragraphs: We work to keep the service reliable but do not guarantee uninterrupted operation. Sync is near real-time but not instantaneous. We may improve, change or discontinue features; if we discontinue the service we will give you at least 30 days' notice and refund any prepaid unused period.

termsSections.title: Disclaimer and liability
paragraphs: To the extent permitted by law, the service is provided “as is”, we are not liable for indirect or consequential damages such as missed appointments, and our total liability is limited to the amount you paid us in the 12 months before the claim. These limits do not apply where the law does not allow them, including liability for gross negligence, wilful misconduct, death or personal injury, or rights consumers cannot waive.

termsSections.title: Suspension and termination
paragraphs: You can stop using the service and delete your account at any time. We may suspend or terminate accounts that seriously or repeatedly breach these terms, with prior notice and an opportunity to remedy where reasonable.

termsSections.title: Open source
paragraphs: The {brand} source code is available under the GNU AGPL-3.0 license. That license governs the code; these terms govern the hosted service. The {brand} name and logo are not licensed for use by forks.

termsSections.title: Governing law
paragraphs: These terms are governed by the laws of {jurisdiction}. If you are a consumer, you also keep the protection of the mandatory laws of your country of residence and may bring claims before the courts of your domicile.

termsSections.title: Changes to these terms
paragraphs: We may update these terms. For material changes we will notify you by email at least 30 days before they take effect; if you don't agree, you can cancel before then. Continuing to use the service afterwards means you accept them.

termsSections.title: Contact
paragraphs: Questions about these terms: {email}.

legal.cookiesIntro: This policy explains which cookies and similar technologies (such as local storage) {brand} uses, why, and how you can control them. It complements our Privacy Policy.

cookiesSections.title: What we use and why
paragraphs: Strictly necessary technologies make the service work (signing you in, protecting against attacks, remembering your language, display preferences and consent choice). The law does not require consent for them, and they can't be switched off.

Optional technologies (browser error monitoring and product analytics) are used only after you accept them in the cookie banner or in Cookie settings, and you can withdraw consent at any time. We do not use advertising or cross-site tracking cookies.

cookiesSections.title: How to control them
paragraphs: Use Cookie settings (in the footer and in Settings → Privacy) to accept, reject or change optional categories. Withdrawing consent stops the optional tools and removes their storage from your browser. You can also block or delete cookies in your browser settings, but blocking strictly necessary cookies will prevent you from signing in.

cookiesSections.title: Changes
paragraphs: When we add a new optional category, we will ask for your consent again.

consent.analyticsBody: Measures how features are used (PostHog) with a pseudonymous identifier, so we can improve the product.
consent.noOptional: This instance doesn't use any optional cookies or trackers.
